text.p: The following are the main stories from Friday morning's Austrian newspapers:
DER STANDARD
- Conservative Foreign Minister Wolfgang Schuessel says Austria has to decide whether or not it wants to join NATO by July 1998 when the country takes over the EU presidency.
- Brickmaker Wienerberger sold its Business Park Vienna complex to real estate fund Immofinanz for three billion schillings. Wienerberger will take a 12 percent stake in Immofinanz.
- Austria's students elected their new parliament. Leftist groups failed to hold on to their majority.
- Far-right Freedom Party criticises new model of politicians' renumeration.
- Austrian pension payments have reached 15.8 percent of the country's gross domestic product.
- Canadian car parts supplier Magna will set up a metal pressing plant for carmaker Chrysler in Austria. The company plans to invest 700 million schillings and create 200 new jobs.

- A conference of labour and industrial representatives says in a report Austria's economy is as dynamic as the U.S. economy. Some one million Austrian employees are changing jobs every year, it claims.

- Bank Austria and Creditanstalt will start their integration process in autumn. With the help of Boston Consulting, the two banks' investment banking arms, their foreign subsidiaries and their treasury operations will be restructured.
- Insurer EA-Generali plans to sell insurance contracts denominated in euros from 1999.
- Austria's Ski Association has suspended top ski jumper Andreas Goldberger for six months after he admitted to having taken cocaine once.
DIE PRESSE
- Postal monopoly Post & Telekom Austria will raise its postal tariffs by July 1. All letters within the EU will cost the same.
- Insurer Wiener Staedtische's chief executive Siegfried Sellitsch says the price for the governent's stake in postal savings bank PSK is too high.
- The Austrian National Bank will reduce the number of its number of governors to four from five currently.
- Troubled machine maker Emco's majority owner Ernst Alexander Maier plans to take over the entire company.
- Bank Austria will raise its 1996 dividend to 12 schillings per share for from ten schillings the year before as group pretax profit inched up one percent to 5.397 billion schillings.
KURIER
- Politicians and psychologists call for stricter gun controls following last week's shooting of a teacher by one of her students.
- The government is pressing employers and employees in the tourism industry to find ways to lower the costs of rising unemployment in the sector.
- Bank Austria is planning to make an exchange offer for Creditanstalt shares in autumn.
- Austria plans to harmonise taxes across the EU when it takes over the presidency in the second half of 1998.
